_README: Copy this file to <SPECIALTY>-<NNN>.json and fill it in. Files beginning with an underscore are ignored by the loader. Run `python -m clinical_simulator.validate` after editing. Every field marked REQUIRED must be present.
title: REQUIRED. Presenting problem, not the diagnosis. The student sees this.
setting: Where the encounter happens, e.g. Emergency department
opening_brief: REQUIRED. Read verbatim to the student. State their role, the patient's age and sex, the presenting complaint and the objective. NEVER hint at the diagnosis.

knows_not: Things this patient genuinely cannot answer. Keeps the patient honest instead of omniscient.
quirks: Behaviours that make the encounter realistic, e.g. minimises symptoms, blames food poisoning.

chief_complaint: REQUIRED. In the patient's own words.

review_of_systems_positive: Things the patient HAS noticed but will only mention if asked.
review_of_systems_negative: Explicit negatives. Without these the patient invents answers to unanticipated questions.

examination.label: Vital signs
aliases: every phrasing a student might use for this manoeuvre
examination.result: The finding, stated factually. No interpretation, no diagnosis.

investigations.label: 12-lead ECG
investigations.result: The result, reported as a report would be.
investigations.note: If appropriate is false, explain here why this test was low-yield or premature. Shown to the evaluator, not the student.

aliases: synonyms and abbreviations the student might write
differentials.why: One or two sentences a marker could read aloud.
excluded_by: REQUIRED for must-exclude items. Ids of examinations or investigations
in THIS case that let a student actually act on the diagnosis.
The validator fails if this is empty or names a finding you did not define.

final_diagnosis: REQUIRED. The full diagnosis including severity and complications.
diagnosis_reasoning: REQUIRED. The reasoning chain, as an examiner would explain it.
critical_clues: Short lowercase fragments matched against the student's own reasoning text. Use word stems, e.g. 'radiat' not 'radiating'.

history.label: What the student should have asked about
history.teaching_note: Why it mattered clinically in THIS case. Shown to the student when missed.

hints: Level 1: point at an area of the case without naming a system.
Level 2: name the pattern or the mechanism, still not the diagnosis.
Level 3: name the topic to review. Still not the diagnosis.
teaching_points: What a student should take away, whether or not they got it right.

evolution.after_action: an examination or investigation id, as an alternative trigger
evolution.update: EVENT: text handed to the preceptor when this fires. Level 4 cases only.

provenance.author: Who wrote it
references: Guideline or textbook the content is grounded in
